text:
The Predators have won three straight, and it isn't smoke: 12-7 on the scoreboard, 54% of the expected goals in those games. Tuesday it was Carolina, 4-1. Thursday in Denver it was overtime, Steven Stamkos finishing it and Vitali Pinchuk scoring his first NHL goal along the way. Stamkos has nine points in his last five games against St. Louis, Filip Forsberg eight, so the Blues know exactly whose sticks to watch.

St. Louis closes a four-game road trip tonight, 1-1-1 so far, and the last two stops were rough. The Blues got 37% of the expected goals in a 3-1 loss at the Rangers and 38% in Thursday's 5-4 overtime loss in New Jersey, where Jesper Bratt won it. They're at 48% at five on five for the season. What has kept them level is Joel Hofer: .918 and 5.1 goals saved above expected, after saving 11 goals above expected last season. Pius Suter is one goal from 100 and one point from 200 for his career, and Justin Barron has eight points in ten, a run that looks earned.

Here is the oddity of the night. Juuse Saros sits at exactly the same +5.1, a season after he was 10.2 goals worse than expected. Over his last five starts he has saved 3.8 above expected and stopped .913 of the hard shots, so this looks like a real recovery rather than a hot week. Both teams have been outchanced more often than not (Nashville is at 46% at five on five), which makes the goaltending matter even more.

Nashville won the first meeting 5-2 on Oct 17 and deserved it in 66% of replays of the shots. Our numbers make tonight close: 3.06 expected goals for Nashville, 2.99 for St. Louis. In the Central, the Predators sit fifth and three points ahead of the sixth-place Blues, with a 51% playoff chance against 34%. A regulation win either way moves that gap a lot for November.
headline: Two goalies at +5.1 and a division gap

hunch.text: Nashville's run is genuine, but a team at 46% at five on five doesn't keep winning by default. Our hunch: Hofer steals the last game of the trip and the Blues win.
